summary: Streaming chat disconnects after session-resume race with duplicate request IDs
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that SSE/WebSocket streaming sessions abruptly close or stop emitting tokens when a client attempts session-resume after a short reconnect window. The pattern appears when client simultaneously retries the last request while the server is processing the final token, leading to a race that leaves the stream in a silent state.

Impact: Multiple FinEdge production customers experience truncated live transcripts in active chats. Business impact: real-time analytics pipelines drop messages; non-critical but high frequency. Estimated ~6% of sessions for this customer over the last 24h.

Environment: prod - us-east; customer is on enterprise plan with session-resume enabled and token-based session IDs.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start a streaming chat (SSE) with long-answer prompt (>800 tokens).
2) Force a short reconnect (simulate flaky mobile/mobile-VPN).
3) Client issues session-resume request within 200-500ms while the original stream still emits final chunks.
4) Client opens a new SSE connection with same session_id and re-sends the last request payload (duplicate request id).
5) Streaming pauses and then connection closes without finalizing generation.

Observed behavior: Stream becomes silent for ~5-30s then connection closed with no final token; no 5xx returned, server logs show request processing complete but no final chunk delivered to resumed connection.

Expected behavior: Session-resume should either (a) gracefully attach to existing in-flight generation and continue emitting tokens to the new connection, or (b) reject resume if in-flight generation finished and deliver final tokens, ensuring at-most-once semantics.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: race between session-manager resume attach and serving-runtime finalization; duplicate request IDs cause session-manager to mark generation as completed without flushing buffered final chunks to the resumed connection. Observed that session-manager drops buffered outbound frames when a resume request with identical request_id arrives while the emitter is mid-flush.

Reproduced in internal staging by replaying customer traffic with a short resume window and duplicate request_id: 3/5 attempts reproduce the silent-close. Root-cause candidate: resume path assumes idempotent resumes by request_id but does not reconcile in-flight emitter state, leading to orphaned output frames.

Telemetry: trace tr-9934 shows serving-runtime finished emission but session-manager did not forward last chunk due to atomic swap of connection handle. No 5xx, so no automatic alert fired.
mitigation:
Short term workaround applied for FinEdge: disabled session-resume feature flag for their org (org-id=fe-org-22) to force new sessions on reconnects; customers informed. This reduced recurrence to 0% for the last 6 hours.

Operational mitigation: increased idle-forwarding window to 60s to allow finishing emission to original connection before a resume attach is permitted. Deployed via config rollout to us-east edge nodes.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation in place (feature-flag off + idle-forwarding window extended). Engineering implemented a server-side dedup/attach patch to session-manager to treat duplicate request_id as idempotent and forward any buffered final chunks to the resumed connection. Patch submitted as PR #4532 and is currently in canary with 10% traffic in us-east. Full rollback plan prepared.

Follow-ups: add an automated test covering resume-while-emitting race; instrument a metric for 'resume-attach-dropped-frames' and add alert; update runbook.
next_steps:
1) Monitor canary for 24h and verify 'resume-attach-dropped-frames' metric at zero for FinEdge traces.
2) If stable, promote PR #4532 to 50% then 100% rollout.
3) Add unit/integration test and include case in nightly regression harness.
4) Postmortem write-up linked to Confluence runbook.
